# Scripts reference (generated)

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_docs.py from scripts/script_catalogue.yaml and the scripts' own code; edit the catalogue, not this file -->

Every script you can run: the entry points in the repository root and everything in `scripts/`. Run all commands from the repository root with the project's Python environment active. **None of these scripts were run to write this page**; each row was written from reading the script's code. Where a row says what a script writes, it says what the code does; where the code could not settle a question the row says so.

How to read it: **Needs IB** says whether the script uses a live Interactive Brokers session (`yes`; `optional` = only for some options; `indirect` = it starts something that connects; `no`). **Writes** is the part to read before running anything. **Flags** are copied from the script's own argument parser (`-` means it takes none or reads them another way; run it with `--help` for the full list).

Why a row changes: the **Flags** and **IB** columns are read from the code on every run, so they cannot drift. The wording in the other columns is hand-checked; each row carries a fingerprint of the script's code, and a test fails when the code changes after the row was checked. **Maintainers:** the hand-checked text lives in `scripts/script_catalogue.yaml`, not in this file; the rule for updating it is in [TECHNICAL_GUIDE.md](../TECHNICAL_GUIDE.md#8-maintaining-the-documentation).

## IB paper probe

Talks to a paper IB account to answer one question; may place orders.

| Script and example | What it does | When to run it | Needs IB | Writes | Flags | Explained in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scripts/probe_w101_combo_close.py`<br>`python scripts/probe_w101_combo_close.py preflight` | Probe of whether a four-leg iron-condor CLOSE fills on the paper account, at what concession over the legs' natural price, and why it does not. It opens a one-lot SPY or QQQ condor (`open`; kinds far, pin and nobid, the last with a long call wing nobody bids for; `--quantity 2` or `3` opens that many lots and `close --quantity N` closes N of them, a staged close that records what the bot's own liveness check says at each size), closes it with the bot's own leg-priced ladder, one new order per rung with a confirmed cancel between them and a clamp under IB's price band (`close`; `--emulate-delay 900` prices each rung from the quotes of 15 minutes earlier, `--require-nobid` insists on an unbid sold leg, `--exclude-unbid` leaves a worthless unbid long leg out of the combo), and records which feed the quotes came from and how the market moved. `flatten` closes by combo, then leg by leg (shorts first). `quotes` shows the legs' bids, asks and feed type. `report` reads the evidence and states a verdict. `open`, `close`, `flatten` and `cancel` PLACE or CANCEL ORDERS. | Only as a deliberate experiment during market hours on a paper account, with the supervisor and the bot stopped (`open`, `close` and `flatten` refuse while data/orchestrator.lock is held, or in market hours while data/bot_heartbeat is fresh). It refuses an account whose id does not start with D, any client id other than 96, and a position or working order on the contracts it would trade that it does not own. Your own positions on other contracts are left alone. | yes | Orders on the paper account (SPY or QQQ, one lot by default and never more than three, every orderRef starts W101PROBE, no combo limit above the wing width); state in reports/w101_probe/state.json and JSONL evidence under reports/w101_probe/&lt;date&gt;/; data/ait_state.db read-only. IB client id 96. `preflight` (the default), `quotes`, `status` and `report` place nothing, and `report` does not connect. A Ctrl-C or an error cancels the probe's working orders and never flattens. | `--quantity` `--data-type` `--spot-hint` `--symbol` `--trial` `--kind` `--short-call` `--rest` `--no-truth-tail` `--require-nobid` `--exclude-unbid` `--emulate-delay` `--legout-only` | - |
| `scripts/probe_w53_roll_atomicity.py`<br>`python scripts/probe_w53_roll_atomicity.py preflight` | Probe of whether IB accepts and fills ONE four-leg cross-expiry order that closes a vertical at one expiry and opens one at another. The subcommands `open`, `roll` and `flatten` PLACE ORDERS. | Only as a deliberate experiment on a paper account. It refuses an account whose id does not start with D, and `open`, `roll` and `flatten` refuse outside regular trading hours. | yes | Orders on the paper account (open, roll, flatten: 1 contract, SPY only); JSONL evidence under reports/w53_probe/; data/ait_state.db read-only. IB client id 97. `preflight` (the default) and `status` place nothing. The subcommand is a positional argument, so it is not in the Flags column. | - | - |
| `scripts/validate_w55_synthetic_delta.py`<br>`python scripts/validate_w55_synthetic_delta.py` | Compares the synthetic per-leg delta with real live option prices from IB on the paper account. | Only as a deliberate check on a paper account (it refuses an account whose id does not start with D) before relying on synthetic deltas. | yes | No orders and no database changes (read-only against the broker); prints a result. IB client id 98. | - | - |

| `scripts/restate_w21_tz_aware.py`<br>`python scripts/restate_w21_tz_aware.py` | Stamps the correct ET offset onto stored naive trade timestamps. Refuses to run if it meets a row it cannot vouch for. | Only on a box whose timestamp migration is still outstanding (see the deploy checklist); stop the bot first. | no | With --apply it snapshots data/ait_state.db to data/backups/ and then UPDATES the timestamp columns of trades, open_positions and exit_outbox. Dry run without the flag. | - | [RUNBOOK.md](../RUNBOOK.md#deploy-checklist-every-deploy) |
